goal: Test establishment/filtering across Izu pollinator-regime geography without treating public-record non-detection as biological absence.

candidate_sources.title: 伊豆諸島の植物誌 第4版
candidate_sources.coverage: Izu Islands flora; expected best candidate for a reviewed multi-island species matrix
candidate_sources.current_access: National Diet Library bibliographic record verified; physical holdings are reported at NDL Kansai, but online full text/species-by-island contents were not recovered through the current public route
candidate_sources.next_action: obtain a lawful readable copy or structured transcription before any modern island-absence analysis

candidate_sources.title: On the Plant Distribution over Izu-Islands
candidate_sources.coverage: nine-island historical phytogeographic study based on island floristic lists; reports 1038 total taxa and selected north/south distribution elements
candidate_sources.current_access: open J-STAGE full article; source reports 103 southern-element and 43 northern-element taxa and further selects conspicuous indicator species
candidate_sources.source_inferred_boundary: southern-element northern limit Miyakejima; northern-element southern limit Mikurajima
candidate_sources.relation_to_focal_boundary: historical broad floristic transition is Miyake-Mikurajima, not Oshima-Toshima
candidate_sources.source_mechanistic_context: article discusses volcanism and Kuroshio position as explanations for the farther-south floristic boundary
candidate_sources.limitation: use only as historical external control for a generic floristic boundary; the paper is not a complete modern species-by-island establishment matrix and includes author-selected indicator groups

candidate_sources.title: An Annotated Checklist of the Vascular Plants of Aogashima Island in the Izu Islands, Japan
candidate_sources.limitation: single-island checklist cannot by itself support the nine-island transition comparison

historical_external_control.focal_result: The source-defined broad north/south floristic transition is placed around Miyakejima-Mikurajima, geographically distinct from the focal Oshima-Toshima pollinator second boundary.
historical_external_control.interpretation: This weakens the narrow alternative that Oshima-Toshima is simply the archipelago's generic whole-flora phytogeographic boundary by definition. It does not rule out local environmental, habitat, dispersal or source-pool differences at Oshima-Toshima.

explicitly_rejected_shortcuts: treat GBIF or iNaturalist non-detection as biological absence
combine unequal public-record effort into an uncorrected island presence/absence matrix
infer native establishment from occurrence coordinates alone
use the 1956 phytogeographic summary or selected indicator taxa as if they were a complete modern species-by-island checklist
minimum_source_matrix_requirements: island-level established/present status from a reviewed flora or checklist
explicit source citation and locality scope
documented handling of historical versus contemporary status

planned_analysis_once_open.primary_question: Are source-resolved high pollinator-dependency mainland lineages less likely than broader-dependency lineages to persist as comparable established taxa across the Oshima/post-boundary geography after area, isolation, habitat and history controls?
planned_analysis_once_open.claim_boundary: Even a reviewed presence/absence matrix would test ecological filtering/establishment, not within-population floral evolution or historical pollinator causation.

claim_boundary: The modern occupancy workstream is intentionally blocked rather than substituting public-record zeros for absence. Historical phytogeographic context is usable and places the broad floristic boundary farther south, but it does not quantify modern pollinator-dependent establishment filtering.
